answer: No dispatch slot opens until its key completes a survey. The board assigns each key a different shale outcrop in the delta. At low tide, a certified scanner records the exposed rock for 12 minutes and signs the cell, tide reading and key. Validators check the full trace before granting one slot and reject reused cells or scans. One honest key spends 12 scanner-minutes. A farm needs 1,000 x 12 = 12,000 scanner-minutes for 1,000 slots if each scanner measures one cell at a time. Rented scanners can parallelize the work. A compromised scanner could sign false traces.
